title.en: To the Tune Linjiangxian: Returning at Night to Lingao

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource; the variant readings it marks are left out and punctuation is added at the source's own phrase breaks.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，删去其所注异文，标点依原文断句补加。

basis.en: Song dynasty lyric (ci); the author died in 1101.

note.en: Another Huangzhou lyric from 1082. Locked out of his own house by a snoring servant, Su Shi stands with his staff and listens to the river, and the small comedy opens into a large wish, to slip away in a boat. A Song anecdote says that the next day word went round that he had sailed off, and the prefect hurried to his house only to find him fast asleep.
note.zh: 同样是 1082 年在黄州所作。家童鼾声如雷，把他关在门外，苏轼倚杖听江声，一场小小的喜剧由此展开成一个很大的愿望：乘小舟从此离去。宋人笔记说，第二天传言他已挂冠乘舟而去，知州急忙赶到他家，却见他鼻息如雷，睡得正香。

excerpt.orig: 敲門都不應，倚杖聽江聲。
excerpt.en: I knock, and no one answers; / leaning on my staff, I listen to the river.
excerpt.zh: 敲门都不应，倚杖听江声。
